turns.prompt_text: what are those weird things that are used to connect two pieces of wood
what are the ones that are made out of wood
turns.response_html:
Commonly referred to as wood joinery, these are various techniques and connections made by shaping the wood itself, often without metal fasteners. Some examples include:

  • Dowel joints: cylindrical wooden pins that fit into holes.
  • Mortise and tenon joints: a rectangular projection (tenon) on one piece fits into a corresponding hole (mortise) on another.
  • Dovetail joints: interlocking, trapezoidal pins and tails create a very strong, often decorative, joint.
  • Biscuit joints: small, oval-shaped pieces of compressed wood are glued into crescent-shaped slots in two pieces.

turns.prompt_text: what are the wooden studs that go into would holes
turns.response_html: Dowel pins are small, cylindrical wooden rods that are used to join two pieces of wood. They are inserted into corresponding holes drilled in each piece and are often used with glue for a strong, hidden joint. Dowel pins can be smooth, but they are often fluted or spiral-grooved to help with glue dispersion and create a stronger bond.

turns.prompt_text: how can you make a fluted dowel out of a smooth towel
turns.response_html:
You can create a fluted dowel from a smooth one using a few simple methods. The goal is to make grooves that allow excess glue and air to escape when the dowel is inserted into a hole.

  • With pliers: Use a pair of pliers with serrated teeth to lightly crimp the dowel along its length. Rotate the dowel and repeat to create a series of small, uniform indentations.
  • With a saw blade: Run the dowel along the teeth of a handsaw or table saw blade. This will score the dowel and create small grooves.
  • With a chisel or knife: Carefully slice a small groove along the length of the dowel with a sharp knife or chisel.
